motion: Is belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God rational given alleged gratuitous evil, salvation confusion, rationality, design, and morality?

routes.description: Establish that belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God is irrational because the available evidence includes apparently gratuitous evil and confused salvation requirements, while the proposed arguments from reason, design, and morality do not adequately support that God.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the conflict between the claimed divine attributes and the observed world, together with epistemic and salvation confusion, defeats or outweighs the cumulative positive case for rational theism.

bridges.description: Given the available reason and evidence, belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God is irrational.

Apparently gratuitous evil and related epistemic confusion outweigh the proposed arguments for God and prevent those arguments from rationally supporting the all-powerful, all-loving God under discussion.
Pervasive suffering that appears to serve no greater good is improbable under an all-powerful, all-loving God, and merely possible theodicies do not make belief in that God rational.
An all-loving God would not attach grave eternal consequences to salvation conditions that sincere people cannot reliably identify and religious communities cannot agree upon.

Evolutionary accounts of cognition and morality, together with alternative explanations of apparent design, undercut the claim that reason, fine-tuning, or moral experience rationally identifies the proposed God.

routes.description: Establish that belief in God is rational through a cumulative case from the reliability of reason, the life-permitting structure of the universe, and objective morality, while answering the evidential challenge from suffering.
routes.successCriteria: Show that rationality, design, and morality are collectively more expected or intelligible if God exists than if God does not, and that suffering does not defeat this cumulative support.

bridges.description: The cumulative available evidence makes belief in God more rational than nonbelief.

The combined evidence from rational minds, cosmic design, and objective morality makes God more probable than God's nonexistence, while available responses prevent suffering from defeating that inference.
Unguided naturalism undermines confidence that evolved minds track truth, whereas an intelligent creator provides a rational basis for trusting human reason and the universe's intelligibility.
The universe's highly specific life-permitting conditions are substantially more probable under intelligent design than under an unguided chance hypothesis.
Objective moral obligations are difficult to ground in an impersonal, purposeless universe but are intelligible when goodness is grounded in God.

sections.title: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason
Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God
Fine-Tuning and Evolutionary Accounts of Design
Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: A belief is rational when it accords with the reason and evidence available to the believer; rationality and truth are therefore distinct questions.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: The world appears filled with suffering that serves no greater good, while belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God requires denying that any such gratuitous evil exists.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: An evil-God hypothesis can reconcile apparent goodness with maximal evil as readily as theodicies reconcile apparent evil with perfect goodness, showing that a merely possible reconciliation does not make either hypothesis probable or rational.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: An all-loving God would not impose grave or eternal consequences for lacking salvation while Christians, Muslims, and Jews cannot reliably agree on which disputed beliefs salvation requires.
moves.sectionTitle: Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: An all-loving God would not create a salvation 'hoop' that appears unlikely, is disputed even by believers, and remains invisible to people who then face eternal punishment.
moves.sectionTitle: Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: If minds result only from mindless, unguided physical processes, confidence in their truth-tracking is self-undermining, whereas an intelligent creator explains why minds and the universe are intelligible.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Natural selection favors advantageous behavior rather than truth, creating a self-undermining reliability problem for unguided evolution that guided evolution avoids because God would intend rational knowers.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: The universe’s physical properties occupy extraordinarily narrow life-permitting ranges whose occurrence by chance is effectively implausible, while their apparent calibration is naturally explained by a super-intellect.
moves.sectionTitle: Fine-Tuning and Evolutionary Accounts of Design

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Objective moral wrongs require explanation, and God is the best explanation because denying objective morality conflicts with deep moral judgments while atheism must otherwise ground moral law without God.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: The arguments from rationality, design, and morality cumulatively make God's existence more probable than God's nonexistence and therefore make belief in God more rational than the alternative.
moves.sectionTitle: Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Attacking atheism does not establish theism; Edwards also conflates atheism with naturalism and has not shown why evolution would favor costly false beliefs over broadly accurate ones.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Evolution need not make cognition wholly unreliable because false representations are often costly, so selection can favor broadly accurate beliefs even though human access to truth remains imperfect.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Theism treats truth as the intended function of human reason, while evolutionary success only sometimes correlates with truth and therefore supplies a weaker basis for trust.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Theism suffers an analogous reliability problem because believers lack access to God’s supposedly mysterious reasoning and must trust that God implanted their access to truth; a shared defect cannot favor theism over naturalism.
moves.sectionTitle: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Suffering and evil are probably the strongest counterevidence to an all-powerful, all-loving God, although Simon denies that they defeat theism.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Christianity affirms the intuition that suffering makes the world other than it ought to be, whereas an atheistic universe of blind indifference cannot affirm that normative judgment.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Assessment of earthly suffering must include an eternal future in which God has resources to restore sufferers and wipe away every tear.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: Recognized defenses involving the best possible world, free will, and soul-making offer serious responses to evil, while Christianity additionally holds that God entered human suffering and can strengthen sufferers and agents who help them.
moves.sectionTitle: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Evolution in a social species explains care, sacrifice, moral intuitions, and the emotional force of religious motifs without requiring theism.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Even granting arguments for a creator, the conflict between an all-powerful, all-loving God and the world's suffering prevents identifying that creator with the Christian God or Allah.
moves.sectionTitle: Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: If God follows independently good standards, morality does not depend on God; if God's commands define goodness, morality becomes arbitrary authority, as troubling scriptural commands illustrate.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: The moral standards used to condemn biblical practices were themselves historically advanced by the Bible's teaching that every person bears God's image and therefore has value and dignity.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Simon Edwards
moves.proposition: The divine-command dilemma is avoided because God neither obeys an external good nor arbitrarily creates goodness: God is the good, and objective value is grounded in the personal creator who set everything in motion.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Identifying God with goodness only restates the dilemma: either God aligns with an independently existing standard or God defines goodness by existing, leaving morality as mere conformity to God.
moves.sectionTitle: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness

moves.speaker: Stephen Woodford
moves.proposition: Before evolutionary theory, biological complexity could rationally suggest creation, but convergent evolutionary evidence now supplies a natural account of apparent design and makes special creation unnecessary even if God could have used evolution.
moves.sectionTitle: Fine-Tuning and Evolutionary Accounts of Design
